finding.symptom: with hdc reverse forwarding the owner gateway WebSocket closes with code 1006 a few seconds after the reader checks and does not reconnect, so the viewer page gets 404 for the index asset
finding.isolation: the same flow over the emulator direct route completes: page served in 16 ms, 9 viewer assets, viewer renders the read-only notice and the session list, stop returns ok
finding.conclusion: the reverse-forwarded long-lived WebSocket is the unstable component, not the LiveShare bundle or the viewer page

verified: the second device reaches the host fixture directly and renders the shared session read-only
share creation, reader refusal/revocation, re-authorization, stop and gateway shutdown pass in this route
caveats: the fixture listens on 0.0.0.0 for the duration of the test (test-only, synthetic identity, random port)
the owner login page still uses the hdc loopback route because ArkWeb only accepts https or 127.0.0.1
